system_description.narrative_title: Nvidia-led AI boom and its systemic risks/opportunities
system_description.narrative_summary: News in this window is dominated by a single narrative: Nvidia’s earnings, guidance and ecosystem moves are the focal point driving a broader AI investment boom, large cloud/data-centre commitments, and a scramble among startups, incumbents and investors. Describe as an open system: capital, compute, talent, data, regulatory signals and geopolitical pressures flow in and out of the AI–chip–cloud nexus, creating reinforcing feedbacks (investment → capacity → demand → valuations) and balancing feedbacks (regulation, labour impacts, supply constraints, competition). The result is cascading effects across markets, corporate strategy, infrastructure buildout and public policy.
system_description.scope: Inside the boundary: AI chipmakers (Nvidia and competitors), cloud hyperscalers and revenue-sharing/cloud partners, AI platform and model startups (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.), data-centre builders/operators and energy suppliers, investors and capital markets, corporate adopters (software, security, hardware), regulators and policy actors, labour/skills markets, and supply-chain partners.
system_description.super_system: Global technology-driven financial and geopolitical system (global economy + strategic tech competition)
adjacent_subsystems: Labor markets & social policy (jobs, reskilling, 'human-reserved' roles)
Capital markets & investor sentiment (valuation cycles, ETFs, banks)
Geopolitical/technology competition (US–China export controls, supply security)
evidence_headlines: Nvidia projects 70% sales growth next year as AI boom shows no sign of slowing
Anthropic and Nscale strike $45 billion cloud deal, sources say
Anthropic expected to tell investors it sees over $30 trillion in potential revenue, WSJ reports
Bill Gates warns ‘there is no plan’ for the ‘upheaval’ AI will cause

variables.name: AI investment rate
variables.description: The continuous rate at which new capital is committed to AI-related assets (hardware, software, data centres, startups and models).

variables.name: AI compute capacity
variables.description: The installed processing capacity available for AI training and inference measured as effective compute power (e.g., FLOPs-equivalent or accelerator-hours).

variables.name: Advanced chip supply pressure
variables.description: The degree of constraint or stress on supply of advanced semiconductor accelerators and related components affecting delivery and pricing.

variables.name: Data-centre buildout rate
variables.description: The pace at which new data-centre capacity (racks, cooling, networking and power provisioning) is planned, constructed and brought online.

variables.name: AI talent availability
variables.description: The size and accessibility of the workforce with AI-relevant skills (researchers, engineers, ops) available for employment or contracting.

variables.name: Training data accessibility
variables.description: The availability and ease of access to high-quality, relevant datasets for model development, transfer and fine-tuning.

variables.name: Regulatory restriction intensity
variables.description: The strictness and scope of legal, compliance and policy constraints applied to AI development, deployment and data flows.

variables.name: Geopolitical sourcing risk
variables.description: The level of geopolitical tension and policy friction that raises risk to cross-border supply chains, market access and technology transfers.

variables.name: Model commercializability
variables.description: The degree to which AI models and platforms can be converted into reliable, scalable revenue streams across customers and use-cases.

variables.name: Valuation expectations
variables.description: The prevailing investor expectations about future firm and asset valuations tied to AI performance and market opportunity.

variables.name: Revenue-sharing prevalence
variables.description: The extent to which commercial arrangements allocate portions of AI-generated revenue across compute providers, platform operators and model developers.

variables.name: Labor displacement pressure
variables.description: The ongoing pressure on existing jobs and required human tasks due to automation and AI-driven process substitution.

variables.name: Energy supply margin
variables.description: The spare electrical capacity, reliability and flexibility available to support growth in energy-intensive AI infrastructure without major constraint.

variables.name: Cybersecurity threat level
variables.description: The intensity and sophistication of cyber risks, including AI-enabled attacks and vulnerabilities, affecting systems and deployments.

variables.name: Market concentration
variables.description: The degree of concentration of market power across suppliers of AI infrastructure, platforms and critical components.

variables.name: Supply-chain lead time
variables.description: The average time lag from order to delivery for critical AI hardware and components across the supply chain.

catalysts.title: OpenAI & Nvidia CEOs speak at G20 tech meeting
catalysts.description: CEOs expected to present and debate international AI norms and coordination, potentially shaping cross-border rules and industry expectations.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'OpenAI, Nvidia CEOs to speak at tech-focused G20 meeting'

catalysts.title: Anthropic–Nscale $45bn data-centre build/rental
catalysts.description: Large contracted AI compute capacity to be built/rented by Anthropic from Nscale, driving rapid data-centre construction and installed AI compute.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Anthropic and Nscale strike $45 billion cloud deal'; 'Anthropic to rent AI computing power from Nscale for $45 billion'

catalysts.title: Nvidia pauses revenue-sharing deals (renegotiation)
catalysts.description: Nvidia's pause on revenue-sharing with AI cloud companies triggers renegotiations and could rewrite commercial economics for cloud-model deployments.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Exclusive | Nvidia Pauses Revenue-Sharing Deals With AI Cloud Companies'

catalysts.title: Nvidia–Hugging Face acquisition and integration
catalysts.description: Nvidia's reported $12.9bn deal for Hugging Face would vertically integrate model tooling and distribution, prompting market and regulatory reactions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, The Information reports'

catalysts.title: Adoption of custom AI chips by major model/cloud players
catalysts.description: Providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, others) advance custom-chip projects, shifting some demand off commodity accelerators and altering supplier dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'OpenAI’s Jalapeño AI chip brings new threat to Nvidia margins'; 'Anthropic in talks with chip start up MatX'

catalysts.title: SK Hynix AI chip output begins in Indiana (2029)
catalysts.description: SK Hynix plans to start AI chip production in Indiana in 2029, expanding U.S. supply of memory/accelerator components.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'SK Hynix to start AI chip output in Indiana in 2029, sees memory shortage through 2030'

catalysts.title: Fed Governor Warsh speech on markets
catalysts.description: A near-term Fed speech could shift interest-rate expectations and thus investor appetite for high-growth AI investments.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Nasdaq, S&P 500 lifted by Nvidia's forecast; investors eye speech by Fed's Warsh'

catalysts.title: 116-company AI cyber-defense push
catalysts.description: Large consortium committed to AI-specific cyber defense could accelerate security standards, procurement and industry coordination.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: ''We have a limited window': 116 companies, entities sign on to major AI cyber defense push'; 'AI’s hacking capabilities are severely underestimated'

catalysts.title: SK Telecom creates AI data‑centre company
catalysts.description: SK Telecom forming a dedicated AI data-centre business will add regional capacity and competitive options for compute and hosting.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'SK Telecom to Create AI Data-Center Company'
